# C Doctest Extract

> Extract C doctest example blocks from a source or Markdown file.

<!-- Section to include introductory text. Make sure to keep an empty line after the intro `section` element and another before the `/section` close. -->

<section class="intro">

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<!-- Package usage documentation. -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```javascript
var extract = require( '@stdlib/_tools/doctest/c/extract' );
```

#### extract( file\[, mode] )

Extracts C example blocks from a file and returns an array of block objects.

<!-- eslint-disable stdlib/doctest -->

```javascript
var blocks = extract( '/path/to/file.c', 'src' );
// returns [ { 'file': '...', 'blockIndex': 0, 'includes': [...], 'body': [...], 'annotations': [...], ... }, ... ]
```

The function accepts the following arguments:

-   **file**: `string` absolute path to the file to parse.
-   **mode**: `string` extraction mode. Must be either `'src'` (default) or `'markdown'`.

When `mode` is `'src'`, the function scans for `@example` blocks inside JSDoc-style `/** ... */` comments in C source files. When `mode` is `'markdown'`, the function scans for fenced ` ```c ` code blocks inside `<section class="c">`, `<section class="usage">`, or `<section class="examples">` sections of Markdown files.

Each returned block object has the following shape:

```text
{
    "file": "/path/to/file.c",   // absolute path of the source file
    "blockIndex": 0,             // zero-based index of the block within the file
    "includes": [...],           // `#include` lines (each: { text, line })
    "staticHelpers": [...],      // file-level `static` declarations (each: { text, line })
    "fileScope": [...],          // file-scope code outside any function (each: { text, line })
    "body": [...],               // executable body lines (each: { text, line })
    "annotations": [...]         // `// returns` comment lines (each: { text, line })
}
```

Blocks are skipped when:

-   the file contains a `// stdlib-c-doctest disable-file` directive (all blocks are skipped), or
-   the function definition immediately following the block is annotated with `// stdlib-c-doctest disable`, or
-   a `<!-- run-disable -->` comment precedes the fenced block, or
-   the fenced block only contains `#include` lines, looks like a function signature, or contains placeholder ellipsis (`...`).

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<!-- Package usage notes. Make sure to keep an empty line after the `section` element and another before the `/section` close. -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   Line numbers in returned objects are **1-indexed** and correspond to actual lines in the source file.
-   Contiguous lines within the same category (e.g., consecutive `body` lines) are merged into a single entry whose `text` contains embedded newlines.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<!-- Package usage examples. -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

<!-- eslint no-undef: "error" -->

```javascript
var join = require( 'path' ).join;
var extract = require( '@stdlib/_tools/doctest/c/extract' );

// Extract blocks from a C source file:
var srcFile = join( __dirname, 'test', 'fixtures', 'src', 'test_edge_cases.c' );
var srcBlocks = extract( srcFile, 'src' );
console.dir( srcBlocks );

// Extract blocks from a Markdown file:
var mdFile = join( __dirname, '..', '..', '..', '..', 'math', 'base', 'special', 'abs', 'README.md' );
var mdBlocks = extract( mdFile, 'markdown' );
console.dir( mdBlocks );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->
